analysis.title: GS Basics: Jensen Back. Commodities/China. Bear Mkt for Inflation
key_insights: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO before the US open Monday and NVDA rose 31.5% in a large short squeeze after shorts were added into the end of last week. Privorotsky asks whether the Trump put is back.
Huang's return reduces doubt about Nvidia's willingness to keep underwriting the AI buildout, and his alignment with the administration may make him lean in harder. CoreWeave rose 22%.
Asia semis rallied hard: Taiwan +9% with TSMC and Foxconn limit up, Kospi +6.5% led by Samsung and SK Hynix, Nikkei +4% on return from holiday.

China barely participated, with CSI 300 +0.14% and Hang Seng -0.73% in early trade. Tighter US rules on remote access to advanced chips are the backdrop, and Commerce licensing for offshore data center access is the first thing to watch.
Congress may turn bipartisan anger into veto-proof support for tougher chip restrictions. Huang testifies Dec. 1.
Chinese 10yr yield at 1.586% is at or near year, 5yr and decade lows, read as a structurally unencouraging signal on China growth and disinflation.

The back end of the US curve barely moved while Nasdaq rose 6.5%. The front end gave back part of Friday's rally and the curve flattened. 2y inflation swaps appear to have slipped through the bottom of their range.

Oil kept sliding with Brent below $90, differentials offered and US refining cracks well off highs. Dubai Dec-Jan backwardation fell from $3.67/bbl in October to $0.16/bbl, with the prompt spread near contango.
The author thinks Iran's grip on the marginal barrel is weakening as more barrels leave the Gulf, and the market is moving toward balance or surplus absent a serious escalation.

Williams was more balanced than Waller or Logan and left successive hikes on the table if data warrant. He sees the tariff impulse fading, energy and AI bottlenecks lifting some prices, little spillover, and inflation falling from about 3.5% this year to just above 2% next year.
December is effectively priced. If commodities keep falling and AI spend questions persist, the author thinks the market starts to trade the last hike of the cycle.

Price action is described as bear market, too violent for anyone to hold. A couple of quiet days would let excess vol premium bleed out and let systematics re-lever, with year-end seasonals as support. Shorts are underwater and are unlikely to have flipped long.

market_movers.rationale: Jensen Huang returned as CEO and the stock rose 31.5% in a short squeeze. His return eases doubt about continued AI buildout funding.
CoreWeave rose 22% as Nvidia's CEO return mattered for AI buildout confidence.
TSMC went limit up in Taiwan alongside the Nvidia rally.

sector_views.rationale: Violent squeeze higher and bear-market-like price action, though the CEO return reduces doubt about AI buildout funding.
Brent below $90, backwardation nearly gone and the market moving toward balance or surplus.

earnings_insights: Dell and Workday earnings are on the watch list this week, with no figures given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: At or near year, 5yr and decade lows, signaling weak China growth and disinflation.
Oil sliding as Gulf barrels flow out, supportive for inflation and rates.
Down from $3.67/bbl in October, the prompt spread is near contango, signaling loosening supply.

macro_indicators.reading: about 3.5% this year to just above 2% next year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Williams sees inflation falling sharply, supporting the case for a last hike.

risk_factors: Violent bear-market-like price action may continue.
Renewed serious escalation involving Iran could reverse the oil decline.
Tougher congressional chip restrictions on China.
Hawkish Fed with successive hikes left on the table.
charts_described: Side-note chart of US 2yr inflation swaps (zero coupon) per Bloomberg, with the text saying it appears to have slipped through the bottom of its range.
vol_and_positioning: Shorts were added into the end of last week and are now underwater after the NVDA squeeze.
Excess vol premium needs to bleed out so systematics can re-lever.
Credit did not have the beta of equities on the day.
Author doubts shorts have already flipped long.
geopolitical: Iran's grip on the marginal barrel is seen weakening as more barrels leave the Gulf, unless there is another serious escalation.
US tightened rules on remote access to advanced chips last week, and Commerce license decisions for Chinese customers via offshore data centers are the first tell.
Congress may build veto-proof bipartisan support for tougher chip restrictions on China, and Jensen Huang testifies Dec. 1.

tension_points.bull_case: Energy and rate impulses are supportive, year-end seasonals are decent, and systematics could re-lever after vol premium bleeds out. Shorts are underwater and have likely not flipped long.
tension_points.bear_case: Price action is bear market, too violent for anyone to hold, and credit lacked equity beta. AI spend questions persist.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A renewed serious oil escalation or lasting AI spend doubts would break the supportive backdrop.
